Stories>Rest is a whole-brain group-level contrast of a social reasoning task (Wason stories presenting social contract, precaution, and descriptive rules). It measures social processing (interpretation of social rules, ToM-related content).
Although stories contain social content, this contrast is not specifically measuring affiliation/attachment (e.g., kinship, cooperation vs stranger); missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1/I2.

The Stories>Rest contrast reflects broad social reasoning and task activation but does not specifically target social communication constructs (reception/production of facial/non-facial communication); missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1/I2.
This contrast does not measure self-perception or self-related judgments; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2.

Although the stories involve reasoning about others, this global Stories>Rest contrast is not a specific test of representing others’ mental states (local evidence for ToM arises in specific story-type contrasts); missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2.

Rest>Stories does not index task-evoked measures of perceiving/understanding others (missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1/I2).

Interpreting social contracts requires exchanging and inferring socially relevant information (intentions, desires) and thus maps onto social communication constructs (receptive/inferential aspects).
The contrast targets inference about others’ mental states in social exchange rather than self-perception; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1/I2.

Social Contracts>Precautions selectively activated ToM-related regions (anterior/posterior temporal, posterior cingulate) reflecting representation and inference about others’ mental states; meets perception-of-others criteria.
